label: Foo fighters
text: Allied aircrews over Europe and the Pacific report glowing objects pacing their aircraft. The 415th Night Fighter Squadron files repeated reports; no Axis weapon is ever identified as the cause.

label: White Sands Proving Ground established
text: Seven days before Trinity, the Army stands up the proving ground that will become the largest military installation in the United States and the geographic centre of the 1947-1951 New Mexico record.

label: Truman creates the Central Intelligence Group and the post of Director of Central Intelligence

sources.text: Presidential Directive on Coordination of Foreign Intelligence Activities, 22 January 1946, FRUS 1945-1950, Emergence of the Intelligence Establishment, Document 71, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1945-50Intel/d71

text: A Presidential directive on the coordination of foreign intelligence activities provides that personnel assigned from State, War and the Navy 'shall collectively form a Central Intelligence Group and shall, under the direction of a Director of Central Intelligence, assist the National Intelligence Authority', the Director to be designated by the President and to sit as a non-voting member of the Authority. Rear Adm. Sidney W. Souers is the first holder and signs as Director of Central Intelligence within two weeks.

label: Project RAND created
text: The Army Air Forces establish Project RAND inside Douglas Aircraft, inventing the contractor-operated analytical partner form that every institution in this domain would later copy.

label: The British-U.S. Communication Intelligence Agreement is signed

sources.text: Outline of British-U.S. Communication Intelligence Agreement, 5 March 1946, NSA UKUSA release copy, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ukusa/agreement_outline_5mar46.pdf

text: STANCIB and the London Signal Intelligence Board sign a twelve-paragraph agreement for unrestricted exchange of the products and methods of communications intelligence. It defines third parties as everyone outside the United States, the British Empire and the Dominions, and states that 'It will be contrary to this agreement to reveal its existence to any third party whatsoever.' A search of all six numbered pages returns no occurrence of flying, saucer, unidentified, aerial phenomen or anomalous.

label: Ghost rockets over Scandinavia
text: Sweden logs hundreds of unexplained rocket-like objects; US and UK intelligence send officers, including Gen. James Doolittle, to assess. No Soviet programme is ever identified.

label: Atomic Energy Act of 1946 makes classification a property of a category

sources.text: Atomic Energy Act of 1946, Public Law 79-585, 60 Stat. 755, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg755.pdf

text: Public Law 79-585, 60 Stat. 755, chapter 724, S. 1717, is approved. Section 10(b)(1) defines restricted data as all data concerning the manufacture or utilization of atomic weapons, the production of fissionable material or its use in the production of power, excluding only what the Commission affirmatively determines may be published. Section 2(a) establishes the Atomic Energy Commission, section 9(a) transfers the Manhattan Engineer District's holdings to it, section 10(b)(4) reaches concealment and destruction with a capital penalty, and section 10(b)(5)(C) gives the FBI exclusive jurisdiction over violations.

label: The Office of Naval Research is created, the same day as the Atomic Energy Act

sources.text: An Act to establish an Office of Naval Research in the Department of the Navy, Public Law 79-588, 60 Stat. 779, approved 1 August 1946, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg779.pdf

text: Public Law 79-588, 60 Stat. 779, establishes an Office of Naval Research in the Office of the Secretary of the Navy, headed by a Chief of Naval Research appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. Section 6 frees its research contracting from five named sections of the Revised Statutes and from performance bonds; section 5(b) keeps obligated research appropriations available four further years. It carries the same approval date as the Atomic Energy Act of 1946 at 60 Stat. 755, not a date two days later.

label: The Armed Forces Special Weapons Project takes effect, holding the military half of the Manhattan Project

sources.text: War Department Memorandum No. 850-25-8, 18 March 1947, reproduced in Appendix D of Defense's Nuclear Agency 1947-1997, DTIC ADA412977, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA412977/DTIC_ADA412977_djvu.txt

text: AFSWP is established by joint directive of the Secretaries of War and the Navy 'effective as of midnight 31 December 1946', operating directly under the Army Chief of Staff and the Chief of Naval Operations and responsible for carrying on the military service functions of the Manhattan Project retained under armed forces control. The founding memorandum is signed on 29 January 1947 by Robert P. Patterson and James V. Forrestal; Major General Leslie R. Groves becomes first Chief on 28 February 1947. Its funds come by working fund advances from the Atomic Energy Commission out of money formerly available to the Manhattan Project.

label: Kenneth Arnold sighting
text: Boise pilot Kenneth Arnold reports nine objects near Mount Rainier. Wire coverage coins 'flying saucer' and the national wave begins.

label: Brazel reports the Foster Ranch debris
text: Mac Brazel reports the debris to Chaves County Sheriff George Wilcox, who calls Roswell Army Air Field. Maj. Jesse Marcel of the 509th Bomb Group and Capt. Sheridan Cavitt of the CIC are sent to retrieve it.

label: RAAF announces possession of a disc
text: Roswell Army Air Field's information office states that the intelligence office of the 509th Bomb Group has gained possession of a disc. The 509th is the only atomic-armed combat group in the world.

label: Ramey retracts the same day
text: Brig. Gen. Roger Ramey displays weather balloon and radar target material at Fort Worth and identifies it as the recovered object. The FBI's Dallas office records the same account by teletype.

label: RAAF press release
text: Walter Haut, public information officer of the 509th Bomb Group, writes and distributes the release announcing that Roswell Army Air Field has come into possession of a flying disc, naming Maj. Jesse Marcel Sr. as the recovering officer. Fort Worth retracts it the same day.

label: RAAF announces a disc, and takes it back the same day
text: 1st Lt. Walter Haut issues the 'flying disc' release; within hours Brig. Gen. Roger Ramey presents the material at Fort Worth as a weather balloon. The Air Force will concede in 1994 that the balloon statement was a cover story.

label: Roswell announces, Fort Worth retracts
text: Roswell Army Air Field publicly announces that the 509th Bomb Group has come into possession of a flying disc. The material is flown to Eighth Air Force headquarters at Fort Worth, where it is presented to the press the same day as a weather balloon and radar target. Four official explanations for the event will follow over the next fifty years.

label: National Security Act signed
text: President Truman signs the National Security Act of 1947, creating the Central Intelligence Agency, the National Security Council and an independent Air Force. The entire institutional architecture within which the UAP record would be created and concealed comes into being seventeen days after the Roswell press release.

label: The National Security Act creates the NSC and the CIA
text: Public Law 80-253, 61 Stat. 495. Section 101 creates the National Security Council; section 102(a) establishes the Central Intelligence Agency under it. Section 102(d)(5), permitting such other functions related to intelligence as the Council may direct, will be the authority for the covert-action charters of 1948 and 1954. The Act creates the National Military Establishment, not the Department of Defense; that renaming comes in 1949.

label: Research and Development Board established
text: The National Security Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 495) creates the Research and Development Board, the statutory coordinating body for defence research. Truman appoints Vannevar Bush its chairman, continuing him from the Joint Research and Development Board the service secretaries had set up after V-J Day.

label: US Air Force established
text: The Air Force becomes an independent service and inherits the flying disc problem, Wright Field, and the Air Materiel Command intelligence apparatus that would run SIGN, GRUDGE and BLUE BOOK.

label: Twining memo
text: Lt. Gen. Nathan Twining writes that 'the phenomenon reported is something real and not visionary or fictitious', and directs consideration of a 'high security project' unknown to his own command.

label: Schulgen collection memorandum distributed
text: Air Force intelligence tasks worldwide collectors on disc-type craft, listing near-hover capability, extreme light weight construction and 'Nuclear propulsion (atomic energy)'.

label: Project SIGN directed
text: On Twining's recommendation the Air Force establishes its first official UFO project inside Air Materiel Command intelligence at Wright Field. It begins operating 23 January 1948.

label: Wright-Patterson and Kirtland are both constituted
text: On the same day the Air Force formally establishes Wright-Patterson AFB, the address of foreign materiel exploitation, and Kirtland AFB, the nuclear weapons and directed energy complex inside Albuquerque.

label: Edgar Albert Fouche born, Americus, Georgia

sources.text: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/180498305/edgar-albert-fouch%C3%A9 ; Library of Congress SRU record LCCN 98002961, http://lx2.loc.gov:210/lcdb

text: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, citing an obituary from Mason Funeral Home, gives the birth date and birthplace. The Library of Congress name authority attached to LCCN 98002961 independently gives 'Fouche, Edgar Rothschild, 1948-'.

label: RAND incorporated as an independent nonprofit
text: RAND separates from Douglas Aircraft and incorporates as a nonprofit, establishing the legal template: permanent, sole-source, answerable to a military customer, outside the civil service.

label: Estimate of the Situation written and destroyed
text: Project SIGN staff conclude the objects are interplanetary. Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Hoyt Vandenberg rejects the estimate for lacking proof and orders copies destroyed. The Condon Report records this twenty years later.

label: Scully's Variety columns
text: Frank Scully publishes two Variety columns describing a recovered saucer and dead occupants, sourced to Silas M. Newton and Leo A. Gebauer.

label: Project SIGN becomes Project GRUDGE
text: The successor project concludes reports are misinterpretation, mass hysteria and hoaxes posing no direct threat to national security, and recommends reducing the scope of investigation.

label: Los Alamos green fireball conference
text: AEC and Air Force personnel, with Edward Teller and Lincoln LaPaz, meet at Los Alamos over the green fireball incursions above the atomic complex. The Department of Energy's institutional predecessor is in the UAP record from the first decade.

label: Nuclear scientists meet at Los Alamos about the green fireballs
text: Edward Teller and Lincoln LaPaz attend a conference on the anomalous objects over northern New Mexico's nuclear installations. LANL's own account records the phenomenon was ultimately dismissed as a national security threat.

label: Los Alamos green fireballs conference
text: Laboratory Director Norris Bradbury, Edward Teller and Frederick Reines meet at Los Alamos with FBI, AEC and military representatives on the green fireballs over the New Mexico nuclear complex. LANL still holds the minutes.

label: CIA Act of 1949 creates unvouchered spending
text: Section 8 of the Central Intelligence Agency Act, now 50 U.S.C. 3510(b), permits Agency sums to be 'expended without regard to the provisions of law and regulations relating to the expenditure of Government funds', with confidential, extraordinary or emergency objects 'accounted for solely on the certificate of the Director'. The oldest and bluntest black-budget instrument in American law, enacted two years after Roswell and never narrowed.

label: Project Twinkle established
text: A network of green fireball observation and photographic stations is stood up over New Mexico. It is never fully implemented and produces no conclusive result.

label: Behind the Flying Saucers
text: Henry Holt publishes Scully's book: a 99-foot disc, sixteen bodies, Hart Canyon near Aztec, March 1948. It becomes a bestseller and supplies the genre's narrative furniture.

label: Guy Hottel FBI memorandum
text: The special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office records a third-hand account of three 50-foot circular craft recovered in New Mexico, each with three three-foot occupants in metallic cloth, attributed to high-powered radar interference. The memo closes: 'No further evaluation was attempted.'

label: Smith writes the 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum
text: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith, Senior Radio Engineer of the Canadian Department of Transport, writes a Top Secret memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications recording what he had been told in Washington: that the flying saucer question was the most highly classified subject in the United States government, rating higher than the H-bomb, and was being worked by a small group headed by Vannevar Bush. Library and Archives Canada quotes the same memorandum's operative line: 'the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence'.

label: A foreign official records the American classification level
text: Wilbert B. Smith, a radio engineer in Canada's Department of Transport, writes an internal memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications stating that the flying saucer subject is classified higher in the United States than the hydrogen bomb and that a small group is studying it. Its evidentiary value is its provenance: a foreign government official reporting internally, not a claimant addressing the public.

label: Project Magnet approved
text: The Canadian Department of Transport approves Smith's request. Project Magnet is the first government programme anywhere whose stated purpose includes applying recovered UAP data to practical engineering.

label: Battelle contracted to Project GRUDGE
text: Capt. Edward Ruppelt creates the contract he calls Project BEAR with the Battelle Memorial Institute to supply scientific support to the Air Force UFO investigation. The first private contractor enters the file.

label: MIT Lincoln Laboratory established
text: Lincoln Laboratory is created to build SAGE, the first continental air defence system - the architecture that determines what American airspace surveillance is built to see.

label: Truman establishes the Psychological Strategy Board by secret directive

sources.text: Directive by the President to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense (Marshall), and the Director of Central Intelligence (Smith), 4 April 1951, FRUS 1951 vol. I doc. 16, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1951v01/d16

text: A directive to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense and the Director of Central Intelligence, classified secret, establishes a Board reporting to the National Security Council for the formulation of over-all national psychological objectives, policies and programmes. Its editorial footnote names the first Director: 'Gordon Gray, President of the University of North Carolina and former Secretary of the Army, was appointed Director of the new board.' The same directive forbids the Board and the Director to perform any psychological operations themselves.

label: UK Flying Saucer Working Party reports
text: Britain's first official body on the question reports and recommends no further investigation - the same self-terminating conclusion Project Condign would reach in 2000.

label: Project Magnet report recommends acquiring the technology
text: Smith's report concludes that 'we are forced to the conclusion that the vehicles are probably extra-terrestrial, in spite of our prejudices to the contrary' and recommends 'a substantial effort towards the acquisition of as much as possible of this technology, which would without doubt be of great value to us'.

label: Battelle contracted for Project Stork
text: The Air Force outsources the statistical analysis of Project Blue Book's case files to Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, under the codename Project Stork.

label: Project Blue Book begins under Ruppelt
text: Capt. Edward Ruppelt renames and professionalises the project, coining the term 'unidentified flying object' to replace 'flying saucer'.

label: Ruppelt briefs the Beacon Hill circle
text: Blue Book director Edward J. Ruppelt gives a 'flying saucer talk' recorded as AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52 - a briefing into the classified summer study on aerial reconnaissance hosted in the MIT/Lincoln Laboratory complex.

label: Project Stork begins
text: Work begins on Project Stork, designation PPS-100, later carried as contract AF-19741, for the Air Technical Intelligence Center. The first status report of 25 April 1952 describes progress 'from its inception on March 31, 1952'. Seven status reports survive, totalling 107 pages, and the transcribing archive records that further reports referenced in the text are not in NARA custody.

label: Project Second Storey established
text: The Defence Research Board establishes a committee under NRC astronomer Peter Millman. It builds a standardised report form with a weighting factor to minimise the 'personal equation', meets six times, concludes UFOs are neither a security threat nor of scientific interest, and recommends ending all Canadian military investigation.

label: Brown files the application that later becomes US 2,949,550, and abandons it

sources.text: US Patent 2,949,550, complete 6-page text, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

text: US 2,949,550 states on its face: 'This invention was disclosed and described in my application Serial No. 293,465, filed June 13, 1952, which application has become abandoned.' This dates the electrokinetic disclosure five years earlier than the filing the board previously recorded as its start.

label: Washington DC radar-visual sightings
text: Unidentified targets are tracked at Washington National, Andrews AFB and the ARTCC over consecutive July weekends, with visual corroboration and scrambled interceptors.

label: Chadwell memo to the DCI
text: CIA's Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence tells the Director that July 1952 produced 250 official reports and that the situation 'contains two elements of danger' with national security implications.

label: NSA established by classified presidential memorandum
text: Truman creates the National Security Agency by a memorandum that is itself classified - the first of the two agencies on this board whose existence was a secret.

label: Newton and Gebauer convicted
text: Scully's two sources are convicted of fraud after millionaire Herman Flader presses charges over 'doodlebug' devices sold on the claim that they used recovered alien technology.

label: The Pentacle Memorandum
text: Battelle's H. C. Cross writes to Miles E. Goll at Wright-Patterson under Project Stork, ref. G-1579-4, SECRET, proposing that 'many different types of aerial activity should be secretly and purposefully scheduled' in areas of high UFO reporting.

label: Robertson Panel convenes
text: A CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence panel sits for four days and recommends stripping UFOs of special status through a mass-media 'debunking' programme, canvassing Disney and the Navy Special Devices Center, and monitoring civilian UFO groups.

label: Robertson Panel convenes uninformed
text: The CIA-convened panel meets five days after the Pentacle memorandum. Per Jacques Vallee it is never briefed on the Battelle proposals - a separate body had already fixed the boundaries of what it could consider.

label: Robertson Panel reports
text: The CIA-convened panel under H. P. Robertson recommends stripping the phenomenon of its 'aura of mystery' through education and debunking, and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups 'because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking'. American UFO information management begins here.

label: The Robertson Panel recommends a debunking programme
text: A CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence panel recommends that the national security agencies strip UFOs of their special status through a programme of mass-media 'training and debunking', and that civilian UFO groups be watched because of their potential influence on mass thinking. This is the documented origin point of the psychological-operations domain.

label: Durant records the proceedings
text: CIA officer Frederick Durant's memorandum to the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence becomes the only substantive account of what the panel actually discussed.

label: The FBI investigates Project Winterhaven as possible fraud
text: An FBI report out of Cincinnati records that Thomas Townsend Brown 'is apparently in Washington attempting to obtain a research and development contract for his so-called Project Winterhaven' and 'anticipates a contract of approximately a million dollars'. The Washington Field Office is directed to determine any possible violation of the Fraud Against the Government statute, and to review Brown's patents at the Patent Office.

label: AFR 200-2 issued
text: The Air Force regulation on UFO reporting restricts public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact that ATIC will analyse the data. Revised 12 August 1954.

label: AFR 200-2 puts the release restriction in writing
text: Air Force Regulation 200-2, short title UFOB, signed by order of the Secretary of the Air Force by N. F. Twining, supersedes AFL 200-5 of 29 April 1952. It designates ATIC as the analysis authority, directs that all evidence be forwarded there, and restricts public discussion to cases conclusively identified as conventional. Identified cases could be discussed; unidentified ones could not.

label: EO 10501 fixes three classification levels and strips 28 agencies of the power to classify
text: Eisenhower signs EO 10501, effective 15 December 1953, revoking EO 10290 of 1951. It limits defense-information markings to Top Secret, Secret and Confidential, removes original classification authority entirely from 28 named agencies and limits 17 more to the agency head. Section 13 leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order, which is where the two classification regimes part company.

label: JANAP 146(C) issued
text: Unidentified flying objects become a mandatory CIRVIS report for airborne personnel, with unauthorised disclosure of report contents prohibited under 18 U.S.C. 793 and 794.

label: NSC 5412 replaces the 1948 covert-action charter
text: The President approves NSC 5412 the day it is circulated. It supersedes NSC 10/2 and NSC 10/5, keeps the authority in section 102(d)(5), restates the plausible-deniability test almost word for word, and makes the Operations Coordinating Board the normal channel for interagency support. It does not create the Special Group; that comes with NSC 5412/2 in December 1955.

label: Atomic Energy Act of 1954
text: Restricted Data is created as a category classified by statute rather than executive order. Any material placed under this authority becomes permanently beyond the reach of presidential declassification directives.

label: The Atomic Energy Act of 1954 makes Restricted Data an Act-wide statutory category
text: Public Law 83-703, 68 Stat. 919, a complete restatement of the 1946 Act. The Restricted Data definition moves out of section 10 and into the definitions chapter as a capitalised category, gains the word 'design', and swaps fissionable material and the production of power for special nuclear material and the production of energy. Removal from the category now runs through the formal procedure at section 142. The phrase 'born classified' appears nowhere in the Act.

label: Battelle's authorship of Special Report No. 14 concealed
text: Battelle completes the statistical study issued as Special Report No. 14 and, per AARO's own history, 'released a report under the cover of ATIC to maintain its anonymity.' Contractor performs, government takes the byline.

label: ATIC and WADC report jointly on a disc-shaped supersonic aircraft

sources.text: TR-AC-47, Joint ATIC-WADC Report on Project Silver Bug, 15 February 1955, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SilverBug/AFD-070114-006.pdf

text: TR-AC-47, Project No. 9961, is issued at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base on the Avro Canada Project Y2 flat-riser. Its stated purpose is to correct the distorted picture presented in previous releases and to alert the intelligence community to any Soviet interest, and its Summary says the project should in no way be associated with any science fiction or flying saucer stories because of its external appearance. It was declassified on 29 March 1995.

label: The CIA establishes the Groom Lake facility
text: Project AQUATONE selects the site because U-2 testing cannot be conducted at Edwards or Palmdale given the secrecy of the project. The first U-2 arrives 24 July 1955.

label: Blue Book Special Report No. 14
text: ATIC issues the largest statistical study of UFO reports ever produced by the US government: 434 of 2,199 objects unknown, with unknown rates rising with report quality.

label: Blue Book Special Report No. 14 issued
text: Battelle delivers the largest statistical study of UFO reports ever performed for the US government, Project No. 10073. The proportion of unknowns rises with the quality of the sighting; the Air Force publicises the opposite conclusion.

label: An aerospace prime proposes an institute to study gravity
text: George S. Trimble of the Glenn L. Martin Company writes to Bryce DeWitt that 'our industry was vitally concerned with gravity' and that respectable researchers 'do not wish to get mixed up in the field of gravity research'. He proposes an 'industrial version of the Institute for Advanced Study'. RIAS, Inc. of Baltimore is the result; Louis Witten is its first researcher.

label: The Institute of Field Physics is incorporated, with an anti-gravity disclaimer written into its publicity

sources.text: History of the Institute of Field Physics (1955-1959), Dean Rickles, UNC Chapel Hill Department of Physics and Astronomy department history, Section II, https://physics.unc.edu/department-history/section-ii/

text: The Institute receives its certificate of incorporation and is placed inside the physics department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill under Bryce and Cecile DeWitt, funded principally by Agnew Bahnson. George Trimble and the Glenn L. Martin Company buy a Founder's Membership for 5,000 dollars. On John Wheeler's insistence a Protection Clause is attached to every publicity statement declaring that the work 'has no connection with so-called "anti-gravity research" of whatever kind and for whatever purposes'.

label: NICAP incorporated in the District of Columbia

sources.text: The UFO Evidence, NICAP, May 1964, CIA filed copy CIA-RDP81R00560R000100010001-0, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp81r00560r000100010001-0 ; FBI file 100-35992, part 1, https://archive.org/details/NICAP

text: The National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena states in its own 1964 volume that it is a non-profit organization incorporated in the District of Columbia in 1956. A Washington Daily News report of 23 October 1956, filed in the FBI's NICAP file, records the organisation forming at 1536 Connecticut Avenue NW under T. Townsend Brown of Leesburg, Virginia, executive vice chairman pro tempore, with a nine-man board of governors still to be elected on 1 November. The District's own corporate register was not opened.

label: RIAS at the Chapel Hill gravitation conference
text: The participants list of the conference on the role of gravitation in physics prints 'Witten, L. | RIAS, Inc., Baltimore' and 'Bass, R.W. | RIAS , Inc., Baltimore'. The conference report is WADC Technical Report 57-216, produced under a funding agreement with the Wright Air Development Center. The participants record their own concern to avoid identification with anti-gravity research.

label: US 2,949,550 filed, Serial No. 669,830, assigned to Whitehall-Rand Inc

sources.text: US Patent 2,949,550, printed header block, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

text: Thomas Townsend Brown of Umatilla, Florida files 'Electrokinetic Apparatus', assignor to Whitehall-Rand, Inc. of Washington D.C., a Delaware corporation. 12 claims, Class 310-5. A private corporate assignee and no government interest statement.

label: CIA resolves to route Keyhoe's UFO inquiries to the Air Force, and to make it a precedent

sources.text: CIA memorandum for record, 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects', CIA reading room document 0005516043, reading-room date 4 April 1958, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0005516043

text: A CIA memorandum for record on 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects' notes that the Air Force was 'most insistent' on answering his letters itself, that 'the Air Force is endeavoring to impress upon Major Keyhoe and others in a similar position, that his office is the proper place to come for such information', and concludes: 'I think we can use this procedure as a precedent henceforth in all inquiries regarding UFO's.'

label: US 3,187,206 filed, Serial No. 734,342, assigned to Electrokinetics Inc

sources.text: US Patent 3,187,206, printed header block, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/fd/fa/17/a3da8c41817315/US3187206.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

text: Thomas Townsend Brown of Walkertown, North Carolina files the second 'Electrokinetic Apparatus', assignor by mesne assignments to Electrokinetics, Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation. 23 claims, Class 310-5.

label: MITRE incorporated
text: The MITRE Corporation is incorporated as a nonprofit, taking Robert Everett and 485 Lincoln Laboratory staff to continue SAGE systems engineering under Air Force sponsorship rather than university administration.

label: Canada-US joint UFO reporting system
text: Library and Archives Canada records that an agreement was finalised between the United States and Canada to institute a joint reporting system for UFOs under CIRVIS/MERINT, 'to extend the early warning coverage for the defence of North America'. Posters depicted a saucer-like object alongside missiles and submarines as examples of objects to be reported.

label: A Study of Lunar Research Flights delivered to the Air Force Special Weapons Center

sources.text: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, DDC AD 425380, https://archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0425380

text: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, by L. Reiffel of the Armour Research Foundation with contributions including C. E. Sagan, is dated 19 June 1959 under Contract AF 29(601)-1164. Its introduction states that the motivation for detonating a nuclear weapon on or near the Moon is threefold, scientific, military and political, and that positive effects would accrue to the nation first performing the feat. Copies went to ARPA at the Pentagon, to the AEC for the Division of Military Application, to Sandia, to Los Alamos, to the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory and to WADD at Wright-Patterson. The string A119 appears nowhere in it.

label: JASON established under IDA administration
text: The government's standing panel of elite scientists is created - and housed inside an FFRDC operator rather than inside the government. It has never been anywhere else since.

label: The first DCI asks Congress to investigate
text: A Worcester Gazette report, filed in CIA records and released in 2014, quotes Adm. Roscoe H. Hillenkoetter, DCI from May 1947 to October 1950: 'The unknown objects are operating under intelligent control. It is imperative that we learn where the UFO's come from and what their purpose is.' He is by then a NICAP board member and has referred his conclusions to the Senate Space Committee.

label: The Aerospace Corporation founded
text: Announced by Lt. Gen. Bernard Schriever, Aerospace is created to provide dedicated technical planning for military space and ballistic missile programmes, with charter restrictions the Air Force had not imposed on earlier FFRDCs.

label: US 2,949,550 granted. The word 'gravity' appears zero times in it

sources.text: US Patent 2,949,550, complete 6-page text, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

text: Claim 1 as granted: 'Thrust producing apparatus comprising an electroconductive body having a relatively large, substantially smooth area thereof exposed to the surrounding medium, an electrode supported on said body, insulated therefrom and shaped to produce a concentrated electrostatic field when electrically charged with respect to said body, and power means connected between said body and electrode to impress high voltage thereon whereby to cause relative movement of an ionizable dielectric medium surrounding said electrodes.' Word counts over all six pages: gravity 0, anti-gravity 0, levitation 0, electrogravitics 0.

label: MOON DUST / BLUE FLY stood up
text: The Air Force establishes a named worldwide capability to collect and exploit unidentified objects and debris surviving re-entry, with a quick-reaction airlift arm routing material to technical intelligence at Wright-Patterson.

label: ATIC is discontinued and the Foreign Technology Division is constituted the same day

sources.text: AEROSPACE TECHNICAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER, Department of the Air Force Organizational Histories compilation, sourced to the Air Force Historical Research Agency, https://www.usafunithistory.com/PDF/A-E/AEROSPACE%20TECHNICAL%20INTELLIGENCE%20CENTER.pdf

text: The Air Force organizational-history record gives a discontinuation and a new constitution rather than a renaming: 'Air Technical Intelligence Center established 21 May 1951; redesignated Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center, 21 September 1959; discontinued 1 July 1961. Foreign Technology Division constituted, activated, and organized 1 July 1961', with the mission and resources absorbed by FTD on that date. The board's prose in more than one node says ATIC 'became' FTD; the record calls it a discontinuation and an absorption. Carried at Tier 2 because the compilation is a private site citing the Air Force Historical Research Agency, whose own pages return 403 to this environment.

label: NRO established as a classified entity
text: The National Reconnaissance Office is created as a joint DoD-CIA activity under a classified directive. Its existence will be an official secret for the next 31 years - the working proof that concealment at agency scale is achievable.

label: An agency whose existence is a secret
text: The National Reconnaissance Office is established with its very existence classified - a status maintained until September 1992. For thirty-one years the legally required answer to whether the organisation existed was no, which is the documented proof that a categorical official denial can be false and lawful at the same time.

label: The Joint Chiefs forward fabricated pretexts for invading Cuba to the Secretary of Defense

sources.text: Memorandum for the Secretary of Defense, 13 March 1962, JCS 1969/321, https://archive.org/download/OperationNorthwoods/operation_northwoods_djvu.txt

label: The Special Group 5412 is renamed the 303 Committee, and nothing else changes
text: McGeorge Bundy signs a two-sentence National Security Action Memorandum renaming the Special Group 5412 as the 303 Committee, expressly altering nothing about its composition, function or responsibility. label: Project Blue Book logs calls from the F. E. Warren base commander

label: Kecksburg
text: A fireball crosses eight states at about 4:44pm EST. Kecksburg residents report an object down in the woods. The Greensburg Tribune-Review reports the area 'immediately sealed off on the order of U.S. Army and State Police officials'. A later edition: 'Searchers Fail to Find Object.'

label: Michigan sightings and 'swamp gas'
text: Mass sightings near Dexter and Hillsdale are met with J. Allen Hynek's provisional swamp gas explanation, reported as a blanket dismissal and met with public fury.

label: First congressional hearing
text: After House Minority Leader Gerald Ford demands an inquiry, the House Armed Services Committee holds a one-day hearing on unidentified flying objects — the first in nineteen years of official investigation.

label: The Low memo
text: Two months before the Air Force contract is signed, project coordinator Robert Low writes that 'the trick would be' to appear a totally objective study to the public while presenting the image of nonbelievers to scientists.

label: The conclusion is written before the study
text: Robert Low's memorandum proposes a study 'conducted almost entirely by non-believers' with 'almost zero expectation of finding a saucer'. McDonald finds it in the project files in July 1967.

label: Lunar Orbiter 1 launched; programme managed by NASA Langley Research Center

text: NASA's NSSDCA master catalogue records the launch of Lunar Orbiter 1 on 10 August 1966, photographic data acquired from 18 to 29 August 1966, and that 'The Lunar Orbiter program was managed by NASA Langley Research Center'. label: Minot AFB documents
text: Three Air Force documents record unexplained aerial activity around Minot AFB, North Dakota, home of the 91st Strategic Missile Wing. Published in facsimile by Robert Hastings.

label: AFR 80-17 assigns the Blue Book effort to the Foreign Technology Division by name

sources.text: Air Force Regulation 80-17, Research and Development - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS (UFO), 19 September 1966, https://nicap.org/afr80-17.htm

Six months earlier the USAF Scientific Advisory Board's ad hoc committee had recorded the resources behind the whole programme as 'only one officer, a sergeant, and secretary'.

label: Condon Committee established
text: The University of Colorado UFO Project is formed under USAF contract 44620-67-C-0035 with Edward Condon as scientific director.

label: All ten Echo Flight missiles lose strategic alert at 0845

sources.text: 341st SMW history, Jan-Mar 1967, p 32, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf

All LF's in E Flight lost strategic alert nearly simultaneously. No other Wing I configuration lost strategic alert at that time.' By about 1400 the same day SAC Headquarters had called in Ogden Air Materiel Area support for a complete engineering analysis.

label: Malmstrom Echo Flight shutdown
text: All ten Minuteman missiles of Echo Flight, 341st Strategic Missile Wing, go off alert status. An Air Force teletype the following day concerns loss of strategic alert. Robert Salas would later attribute the cause to an object over the front gate.

label: The engineering investigation reports it cannot determine a cause

It is footnoted on almost every page of the wing history's Echo Flight section and has never been opened by this board. Through the history it states: 'The investigation teams at Malmstrom, were unable to determine a logical cause for the incident.'

The conclusion follows from a run of negative tests rather than from reproducing the event in the field.

label: The 1127th's own history names the recovery pipeline
text: The 1127th USAF Field Activities Group's semiannual history, doc. AFNIABA 014-67, lists Project BLUE FLY, MIG-17 Exploitation and Project MOON DUST together under FOREIGN MATERIEL PROGRAM. It records exploitation personnel from FTD Detachment 3 deployed to crash sites and about three tons of parts airlifted to Wright-Patterson, and SPADATS notifying the unit of 37 Soviet deorbits.

label: Shag Harbour
text: An object enters the water off Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia at about 11:20pm ADT before at least eleven witnesses. RCC Halifax telexes the RCAF Air Desk in Ottawa having eliminated all aircraft; the Navy tasks Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic to a three-day underwater search. Nothing is found.

label: AEC detonates 29 kilotons at 4,227 feet, twelve miles from Dulce

sources.text: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

text: The US Atomic Energy Commission detonated a 29-kiloton-yield nuclear device in the emplacement well GB-E at a depth of 4,227 feet, twelve miles southwest of Dulce in the Carson National Forest, to stimulate natural gas production from the Pictured Cliffs Formation. The first reservoir-stimulation experiment of the Plowshare programme, jointly sponsored by the AEC, the Department of the Interior and El Paso Natural Gas. THE EARLIEST DATED ARTEFACT IN THE CLUSTER, and it is a government record, twelve years before the rumour begins.

label: McDonnell Douglas funds an internal study
text: Robert M. Wood begins a company-funded study of unidentified craft and their propulsion at McDonnell Douglas Astronautics, Huntington Beach. No government contract, no reporting obligation, no released record.

label: Look publishes 'Flying Saucer Fiasco'
text: John G. Fuller publishes the Low memo, calling the project a $500,000 trick. Condon fires investigators David Saunders and Norman Levine.

label: House Science Committee UFO symposium
text: Hynek, James McDonald, Carl Sagan and others testify. McDonald tells Congress that 'credible observers are observing relatively incredible objects'. No legislation follows.

text: Ground radar, base weather radar, airborne radar and visual observation converge on an object near B-52H JAG 31; the bomber's transmitter fails for four minutes; Minuteman sites of N, O, J and M Flights report alarms and an inner door combination lock moved. Blue Book sends no field investigators.

Werlich of the 862nd Combat Support Group Operations Division prepared eight pages of Basic Reporting Data on the 24 October 1968 Minot events and transmitted it to multiple Air Force agencies. Seven airmen completed AF Form 117 questionnaires, thirteen B-52 ASQ-38 radarscope photographs were printed with data plates, and Werlich drew an overlay map at 1:200,000. Every witness statement in the file is contemporaneous and official.

label: RAND publishes 'UFOs: What To Do?'
text: George Kocher's draft DRU-1571 examines UFO brightness, size and manoeuvres and recommends a course of action - two months before the Condon report tells the public the subject is closed.

label: The Condon Report closes the official file
text: The University of Colorado study directed by Edward Condon publishes 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects', including Martin Altschuler's chapter on atmospheric electricity and plasma interpretations. Project Blue Book is terminated the following year, ending official American investigation for the next four decades.

text: 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects' concludes further study is unwarranted, while its Section V Chapter 2 documents the 1948 Estimate of the Situation and its destruction.

text: Brig. Gen. Carroll Bolender recommends terminating Blue Book, explaining that UFO reports affecting national security go via JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and 'are not part of the Blue Book system'.

label: Secretary of the Air Force terminates Project BLUE BOOK
text: After 12,618 reported sightings of which 701 remain unidentified, the Air Force closes its public UFO channel on the strength of the Condon Report and a National Academy of Sciences review. No document terminating classified collection is ever produced.

label: Project Blue Book terminated
text: Secretary of the Air Force Robert C. Seamans Jr. closes the program citing the Condon Report. Final tally: 12,618 sightings, 701 never identified.

label: Blue Book is terminated on the Condon findings
text: The Air Force closes its public reporting channel citing the University of Colorado report. The Bolender memo of the same period records that reports affecting national security were never in that channel.

text: The CIA initiates 'scan by coordinate' in response to assessments of Soviet psychotronic spending. SRI research under Puthoff and Targ follows in 1972.

text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin the SRI International programme that becomes the government's Stargate effort - the template for outsourcing an unwanted phenomenon to a private laboratory.

label: CIA funds SRI psychoenergetics
text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin CIA-funded remote-viewing research at Stanford Research Institute - the start of a 23-year compartmented programme in a publicly ridiculed domain.

label: Federal funding of anomalous cognition begins
text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin remote viewing work at Stanford Research Institute under federal sponsorship. The programme runs through Grill Flame, Center Lane, Sun Streak and Star Gate until 1995, establishing beyond argument that the US government funds research of this kind for decades at a time before terminating it and denying it produced anything.

label: EO 11652 puts classified material on an automatic declassification timetable
text: Nixon signs EO 11652, effective 1 June 1972, superseding EO 10501 and six amending orders. It creates the General Declassification Schedule, under which Top Secret declassifies after ten years and Confidential after six, adds a thirty-year rule that only a Department head can override in writing, and creates an Interagency Classification Review Committee under the NSC that takes complaints from outside the government.

text: The advisory panel's administration transfers between FFRDC-adjacent operators for the first time, establishing the pattern of contractor custody of the government's most sensitive scientific advice.

label: Targ and Puthoff publish in Nature
text: 'Information transmission under conditions of sensory shielding' appears in Nature vol. 251, pp. 602-607 - the open-literature face of a classified programme.

label: The USIB charters a standing committee tasked with anomalies by name

label: Ben Rich takes over Skunk Works
text: Rich succeeds Kelly Johnson as director of Lockheed's Advanced Development Projects, holding the deepest black-aerospace access available to a private citizen for the next sixteen years.

label: Loring AFB overflights begin
text: Unidentified aerial incursions are logged over Loring AFB, Maine, opening a three-week sequence across SAC nuclear installations.

text: At 0605 EST on 29 October 1975 the National Military Command Center issued a Memorandum for Record subject 'AFB Penetration', signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations, recording that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB in proximity to a weapons storage area, that an Army National Guard helicopter had failed to locate it, and that NORAD had obtained Canadian authority to pursue across the border. Distribution ran to CJCS, DJS, J-30 through J-38, the service chiefs and the DIA, NSA and CIA representatives.

label: A KC-135 pursues an object from the Wurtsmith weapons storage area over Lake Huron

sources.text: NICAP, 'Wurtsmith and Others', http://www.nicap.org/articles/CI-Wurtsmith.htm

text: The NORAD Senior Director's Log for 31 October 1975 records: 'Alerted by NCOC of a helicopter sighted over Wurtsmith AFB Wpns storage area, a tanker sighted same and pursued it 35 SE over Lake Huron.' A Joint Chiefs of Staff operational report of 30 October 1975 records that the Michigan Department of Natural Resources was contacted about aircraft searching for hunters spotting deer, and the explanation did not fit.

label: Malmstrom AFB and Minuteman fields overflown
text: DoD records later released under FOIA case 97-F-1677 describe numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom AFB and its missile fields, which multiple F-106 interceptors could not acquire.

label: Two F-106s scrambled over the Malmstrom missile field; radar contact lost

sources.text: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt

text: The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 8 November 1975: height-finder personnel picked up objects at 10,000 to 13,000 feet on track J330; two F-106s were scrambled at 0754Z; at 0820Z 'Lost radar contact, fighters broken off at 0825'; at 0905Z 'L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects'; and at 0915Z, from four different points, 'when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on'.

label: NMCC memorandum for the record
text: At 0253 EST Malmstrom takes seven height-finder radar cuts between 9,500 and 15,500 feet with simultaneous ground witnesses; FAA cross-tell shows no jet within 100NM; two F-106s are scrambled at 0254 and airborne at 0257; at 0344 the objects cannot be intercepted.

label: CINCNORAD summarises the sequence across five installations

sources.text: NICAP, quoting the CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975, http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm

text: 'Since 28 Oct 75 numerous reports of suspicious objects have been received at the NORAD CU; reliable military personnel at Loring AFB, Maine, Wurtsmith AFB, Michigan, Malmstrom AFB, Mt, Minot AFB, ND, and Canadian Forces Station, Falconbridge, Ontario, Canada have visually sighted suspicious objects.' The message names Minot AFB where the 24th NORAD Region's own log had named Minot Air Force Station the day before.

label: NORAD summary document
text: A NORAD document records that reliable military personnel at Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot and CFS Falconbridge had visually sighted suspicious objects during October and early November 1975.

label: The NORAD log closes the Malmstrom sequence

sources.text: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 19 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt

text: '19 Nov 75 (1327Z) - SAC command post report UFO observed by FSC & a cook, observed object travelling NE between M-8 and M-l at a fast rate of speed. Object bright white light seen 45 to 50 sec following terrain 200 ft off ground. The light was two to three times brighter than landing lights on a jet.' The original marks this as the last entry pertaining to these incidents.

label: Gabe Valdez stationed at Dulce, begins the livestock investigations

text: A New Mexico State Police officer stationed in Dulce in 1976 began investigating cattle and other animals found dead with soft tissue removed, and became the central official figure in the region's caseload. The only official investigator anywhere in this story.

label: IHEDN committee opens the French file
text: A committee of the Institut des Hautes Études de Défense Nationale chaired by General Blanchard of the Gendarmerie Nationale opens the unidentified flying objects file with the objective of proposing how to organise research and data collection. Its recommendations are adopted.

label: Church Committee files Book I and records that it never examined an agency file itself

text: Senate Report 94-755, Book I, Foreign and Military Intelligence, is filed. Its section on the obstacles the committee met states that despite its legal Senate mandate and the issuance of subpoenas, in no instance had the committee been able to examine the agencies' files on its own. Its publication note records that three chapters, Cover, Espionage and Budgetary Oversight, were deleted at the request of the agencies.

label: GEPAN created inside CNES
text: The French national space agency establishes GEPAN under Claude Poher with the authority of director general Yves Sillard - the world's first and still only permanent civilian government UAP office with a public case archive. The Gendarmerie Nationale routes sighting reports to it by teletype.

label: CAUS founded
text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy is established under attorney Peter Gersten and begins FOIA litigation against the CIA.

label: JANAP 146 still lists UFOs, eight years after Blue Book closed
text: Change No. 2 to JANAP 146(E) is promulgated. Unidentified flying objects remain a reportable CIRVIS category at Article 201, and Article 208 continues to incorporate 18 U.S.C. 793 and the Canadian Official Secrets Act. Project Blue Book closed in December 1969. The document was released under FOIA on 28 February 1994.

label: The Petrozavodsk phenomenon
text: A luminous object is reported from Copenhagen and Helsinki to Vladivostok. Northern European governments write to the president of the USSR Academy of Sciences asking whether it was Soviet weapons testing. The Academy's own preliminary report concludes that 'based on the available data, it is unfeasible to satisfactorily understand the observed phenomenon'.

label: Operação Prato begins on Colares
text: The Brazilian Air Force and the National Information Service open the first Brazilian military operation mounted solely to investigate UAP, at the request of the mayor of Colares after residents report burns and puncture wounds from descending lights. Captain Uyrangê Hollanda commands.

label: HAVE BLUE flies at Groom Lake
text: Lockheed's stealth demonstrator first flies from a facility whose existence the government will not acknowledge for another twenty-one years.

label: Council Bluffs fall
text: Five independent witness groups see a luminous mass descend near Big Lake Park, Council Bluffs, Iowa; police photograph a four-by-six-foot molten metal mass. The sample survives into the modern literature.

label: CAUS FOIA request
text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy files for the Loring, Wurtsmith and Malmstrom case files. On 6 February 1978 the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense identifies twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents; after an internal dispute Assistant Secretary Thomas Ross orders the withheld fifteen released.

label: AEC decommissions the site and injects liquid radioactive waste into the cavity

sources.text: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

text: Structures and equipment were decontaminated and removed, liquid radioactive waste was injected into the former cavity now forming the lower part of the collapse chimney, solid radioactive waste went to the Nevada Test Site, and test wells were plugged. Soil sampling followed in 1978, 1986, 2000 and 2002.

label: GRILL FLAME formalised
text: Army INSCOM and DIA formalise operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using SRI methodology - the first of four codenames for one continuous seventeen-year effort.

label: First Council Bluffs analysis
text: The Des Moines Register reports the initial materials analyses identifying the metal as high-carbon steel and slag - the baseline the 2022 Stanford work would revisit.

label: Friedman meets Marcel
text: Stanton Friedman is put in touch with retired Lt. Col. Jesse Marcel Sr. in Baton Rouge. Marcel states the weather balloon account was a cover and that the material was not of this earth. Roswell restarts after thirty-one years.

label: Jesse Marcel breaks silence
text: The 509th's intelligence officer tells researcher Stanton Friedman that the 1947 weather balloon explanation was a cover story, restarting the Roswell inquiry after thirty-one years.

label: GEPAN's classified five-volume report
text: GEPAN reports to its scientific council in five volumes and about 500 pages, limited to 120 or 140 copies and secret. Of eleven high-strangeness cases studied by four-person teams including psychologists, ten were concluded to be material phenomena not explicable as natural or human. A document in the US NSA's declassified UFO collection assesses that its method makes 'the bulk of the Condon Report seem very poor by comparison'.

label: EO 12065 requires the public interest in disclosure to be weighed
text: Carter's classification order revokes EO 11652 and, at section 3-303, requires an official to determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security. It is the only classification order to have carried such a test, and it lasts four years.

label: Retrievals of the Third Kind
text: Leonard Stringfield delivers Status Report I at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton, Ohio. The crash-retrieval literature begins as a research field.

label: Founding meeting of SETKA at the USSR Academy of Sciences
text: Migulin and Platov of IZMIRAN, Narimanov and Petrovskaya of the Institute for Space Studies, Balashov and Volga of secret military unit 67947, Gindilis of the Shternberg Institute and others meet. SETKA-AN and SETKA-MO are established on the order of the Military-Industrial Commission. The official history later gives as one reason for secrecy the possibility 'that some of the UFO characteristics could be used for military purposes'.

text: GAO-04-332, 'Industrial Security: DOD Cannot Provide Adequate Assurances That Its Oversight Ensures the Protection of Classified Information', prepared in response to a Senate report accompanying the FY2004 NDAA. DSS monitored 11,000-plus contractor facilities; GAO issued seven recommendations. text: GAO-04-332 finds that DoD 'cannot provide adequate assurances that its oversight ensures the protection of classified information' at more than 11,000 cleared contractor facilities. text: Princeton vectors two VFA-41 F/A-18Fs to a contact it has held on Aegis for two weeks. Fravor, Dietrich and their WSOs watch a 46-foot white object for about five minutes; it departs and reappears at the CAP point 60 miles away in under a minute. A follow-on sortie records FLIR1.

text: The Navy range fouler report on the incident records: 'Pilots reported the incident through Intelligence Personnel. Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.'

text: Three Princeton crewmen in different divisions - Day, Voorhis and Turner - describe unidentified personnel coming aboard within roughly 48 hours and removing or ordering wiped the recording media. No FOIA release, visit log or message traffic has ever identified them.

text: Senator Harry Reid, prompted by Robert Bigelow, sets in motion the program that becomes AATIP. Funding of roughly $22 million flows from late 2008 through 2011, most of it to Bigelow Aerospace.

text: Judge Sullivan holds that NASA 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate', denies summary judgment in part, and orders the parties to propose search and documentation procedures creating a proper record. text: Section 1687 of the FY2024 NDAA bars funds for UAP activity under special or restricted access limitation absent disclosure to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership, and provides that 'independent research and development funding relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena shall not be allowable as indirect expenses'. The Review Board, the eminent domain clause, the Controlled Disclosure Campaign Plan, the $20,000,000 authorization, the contractor turn-in and the immunity grant are all gone. Sec. 7343 is left referring to an instruction it no longer identifies.

text: As of August 2026, more than two years after Volume I promised further findings, the second volume of AARO's historical record report has not been released.

label: State of the record, August 2026
text: The retrieval literature stands where Stringfield left it: a large, internally consistent, unauditable testimony corpus. The nuclear-incursion strand stands materially higher, on FOIA-released NORAD, NMCC and Air Force paper plus named affiants. The only judicial findings in the domain are that a UFO injury claim fails on the pleadings and that a UFO records search was inadequate.

label: Twenty-one months of silence on Immaculate Constellation
text: No AARO annual report, statement for the record or PURSUE tranche has addressed a programme name entered into the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024. The Department's position remains 'no record'.

label: Eleven months, no UAP hearing
text: Between 9 September 2025 and 12 August 2026 - covering the February 2026 release directive, five PURSUE tranches, the late FY2025 annual report, the NDA waiver and the Burlison amendment - Congress holds no hearing on UAP.

label: State of play
text: MITRE's 45-day unclassified production deadline has passed with no public production; no letter has been made public to RAND, Aerospace, IDA or Sandia; the FY2027 NDAA contractor-records provision awaits the Senate.

label: Historical Record Report Volume II remains unpublished
text: Promised within months in November 2024, said in June 2025 to carry the Yankee Blue findings and scheduled for late 2025, and absent from AARO's Congressional and Press Products page on 12 August 2026 - after five PURSUE tranches and an IC-wide NDA waiver.

label: Five agencies ordered to release UAP information have no series in the statutory archive
text: CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA and DOE are addressees of ODNI ES 2026-00818 and absentees from Record Group 615. NARA publishes no compliance list and no statement identifying non-compliant agencies.

label: Reckoning scheduled for publication
text: Elizondo's second book, promising 'previously undisclosed evidence', is scheduled for HarperCollins release with a 20-date speaking tour. Its DOPSR status is not yet public.

label: Air Force becomes the first military department to transfer into RG 615
text: The National Archives accessioned 'Records from the Department of the Air Force Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena' (catalog series 656595571, accession TR-0615-2026-0003) into Record Group 615: 30 PDF files dated 25 October 1945 to 31 December 1969, access and use both Unrestricted, carrying contiguous UAP Record Identifiers 342UAP00001 to 342UAP00030. It is the eighth agency series in RG 615 and the first from a military department in its own right. The documents' own declassification blocks show the Air Force Declassification Office cleared them on 5 May 2025 under the FY24 NDAA authority now codified at 44 U.S.C. 2107, fifteen months before the records reached NARA.

label: The Ellsworth claim is published with both witnesses, and contradicts its own recording

text: Jesse Michels published video rjUdn6FklAU, 2:47:21, presenting Mario Woods and Michael Johnson on the 18 November 1977 Launch Facility November-5 claim. Its on-camera retelling of the moment of recognition at 00:17:46-00:18:11 says Johnson recognised the event with nothing supplied; its own recording of that moment at 00:07:29-00:07:46 shows an initial 'No', then Woods naming the UFO twice, then assent. Both passages are timestamped in the same episode. This is the dated artefact on which the claim rests.

label: Scheduled: DCSA NISP oversight phase-out
text: DoDI 5205.11 para 1.2.i: 'Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversight for the administration of the National Industrial Security Program will be phased out in July 2029 in accordance with the carve-out provision.' Forward-dated commitment recorded in a 12 September 2024 issuance.
